title: Finite-type reduced toric realizations and their smooth tori
statement: Let $M$ be a fine torsion-free monoscheme admitting a finite affine cover, and form $X=\mathbf Q[M]$ with its component tori and coactions as in [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization]. Then $X$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] and of finite type over $\mathbf Q$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. It has finitely many connected components, each integral. On each component the generic group $L$ is a finitely generated free abelian group of finite rank $r$, and $T=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Q[L]$ is isomorphic as a group scheme to $\mathbf G_m^r=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Q[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_r^{\pm1}]$, with multiplication and unit given by multiplying coordinates and the coordinates $1$. In particular $T$ is a smooth finite-type $\mathbf Q$-group [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] acting on that component by the indicated coaction. For every reduced finite-type $\mathbf Q$-scheme $Y$, $T\times_{\mathbf Q}Y$ is reduced and of finite type, and its projection to $Y$ is smooth and surjective. The assertions about reducedness, finite type and finitely many components also hold for finite disjoint unions of such realizations.

proof.text: Apply finite_chart_components_realization over ULift Q and finite_chart_components_algebra. The first gives reducedness, local finite type, quasi-compactness, finitely many connected components, their component inclusions and integrality. Surjectivity of its component equivalence supplies the requested component for each D. The second supplies a finite lattice-coordinate equivalence for each component.

proof.text: For the resulting rank r and coordinate equivalence b, latticeTorus_coordinates supplies the required group-scheme isomorphism and latticeTorus_finiteType supplies finite type and quasi-compactness of the torus and its products with finite-type bases. The defining choice specification of existsUnique_torusAction gives the canonical chart formula. Apply the component action-laws lemma to this component of the arbitrary ambient M to obtain ModObj; unlike latticeTorus_action this does not require the ambient M to be connected.

source.place: Expose VIII, Proposition 3.2.2 and 3.2.4, printed p.103; chartwise action and gluing on a single connected component.

proof.text: The field ULift Q has characteristic zero: apply ULift.down to an equality of natural-number casts and use injectivity of casts in Q. The lattice finite-type theorem supplies local finite type of each torus, and its canonical Hopf structure makes it a group scheme. Cartier smoothness, via the already closed adopted source declaration smooth_of_grpObj_of_charZero, gives smoothness of its structure morphism. This route uses the specific rational base and avoids the additive-lattice transport and the separate split-projection theorem. Smoothness is stable under base change. Smooth morphisms are flat with geometrically reduced fibres. A finite-type Y over Q is locally Noetherian; the Mathlib flat geometrically reduced pullback theorem therefore gives reducedness of the product. The Hopf counit defines an augmentation section of the torus structure map: counit_algebraMap shows its composite with that structure map is the identity. Pair this section after fY with the identity on Y in pullback.lift. The second projection retracts this section, so it is surjective on points. The torus-product finite-type conclusions still come from latticeTorus_finiteType as in Step 2. Rank zero and empty Y require no exceptions.

source.place: Theorem 3.23 (Cartier), printed p.71, via the adopted source theorem smooth_of_grpObj_of_charZero. Smooth reduced fibres: Stacks 056T; reduced flat base change: Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry/Geometrically/Reduced.lean:119-125; the augmentation section is the unit in ILO VIII 3.2.4.

proof.text: For a finite family, apply the already stated realization result to each member. Mathlib IsReduced.of_openCover for sigmaOpenCover gives reducedness. IsZariskiLocalAtSource.sigmaDesc gives local finite type. Each summand is compact because its structure map is quasi-compact over the compact affine base. The finite summand open cover is therefore compact; quasiCompact_of_compactSpace gives quasi-compactness of the coproduct structure map. The disjoint union of the finite connected-component sets maps to the connected components of the coproduct by the maps induced by the summand inclusions. This map is surjective: choose a point of a component and then a preimage in a summand using sigmaOpenCover.exists_eq. Finite.of_surjective gives finiteness, also for an empty family.

proof_origin.place: ILO VIII 3.2.2 and 3.2.4 for components and actions, combined with the declared finite-chart and coordinate results. Smoothness uses the shorter rational-base route through Cartier (Milne Theorem 3.23), the already closed source declaration. Product reducedness uses smooth geometrically reduced base change; surjectivity uses the explicit counit section. The finite coproduct argument and these combinations were written by G6.
